text:
maya (infra): Heads up, seeing a weird scheduler pattern in west-1 GPU pool — ~60% of GPUs idle while a handful are at 100% and queue keeps growing. Admission queue sits at 482 pending and dispatch lag spikes to 6-8s.

leo (serving): do you have a job id / dashboard link?

maya (infra): job id job-7892, dashboard: https://grafana.internal/clusters/west-1/gpu-pool?panel=dispatch-lag — spike started ~10:02 UTC. Looks like a stream of tiny tasks from a single batch job is holding the admission window open, preventing other workloads from scheduling.

darren (scheduler): curious — could be the allocate_slots token leak we saw in q2. Any preemption logs or slot-release failures?

maya (infra): attaching a short tail of scheduler logs:
```
2026-03-18T10:02:14Z INFO admission_queue size=482 rate_limit=50/s dispatch_lag_ms=6100 top_job=job-7892 tasks_in_flight=120
2026-03-18T10:02:15Z WARN allocate_slots failed: timeout waiting for slot_release for job=job-7892 task=5312
2026-03-18T10:02:16Z INFO dispatcher skipped=37 head_of_line=job-7892
```

anna (ml infra): job-7892 is the nightly eval runner that shards tons of 1-2s tasks. We usually set concurrency low but looks like a recent config/rollout bumped concurrency per-shard. Could be correlated.

sre-bot: [ALERT] High dispatch_lag detected in west-1-gpu-pool, threshold=2000ms, current=6200ms — incident created: INC-20260318-72

darren (scheduler): I can reproduce locally with a synthetic that submits thousands of tiny tasks to the same job id. The scheduler's per-job inflight counter isn't decrementing in the allocate_slots error path. Quick repro snippet:
```bash
# repro script (simplified)
for i in $(seq 1 5000); do
  curl -s -X POST /api/v1/submit -d '{"job":"job-repro","task":"'$i'","duration_ms":200}' &
done
```

darren (scheduler): proposed immediate fix is to ensure allocate_slots has a finally/cleanup path to release the inflight token when a task fails to start. Will PR a small hotfix.

maya (infra): need a mitigation we can apply now — can we lower max_inflight_per_job or throttle that job? Also want to avoid full redeploy of scheduler during peak.

ops-oncall: I'm applying an admission throttle for job-7892 and lowering max_inflight_per_job to 40 for west-1 as a temporary measure. Commands run:
```
redwoodctl admission throttle set --job job-7892 --rate 10/s --cluster west-1
redwoodctl pool config update west-1-gpu-pool --max-inflight-per-job 40
```

ops-oncall: isolated the job to a low-priority routing rule and drained 8 busy nodes — routing change should allow other jobs to get slots.

maya (infra): thanks — metrics improving: admission_queue down to 28, dispatch_lag ~350ms, overall GPU util evened out. Will watch for the next 30m. :thumbsup:

darren (scheduler): hotfix PR opened and tests added to cover the allocate_slots failure path. I'll ping infra for canary deploy to a single scheduler instance and watch. PR: https://phabricator.internal/D1234

anna (ml infra): also rolling the eval runner config back to previous concurrency for the nightly until we confirm scheduler fix. I'll open a changelog entry.

leo (serving): can we capture cost impact for the spike? Looks like wasted partial-minute billing on 8 nodes. Rough estimate: ~8 nodes * $2.4/hr * 0.5hr => ~$9.6 — not huge but we should prevent recurrence.

darren (scheduler): follow-up items: 1) backport hotfix to release branches, 2) add a unit test and an integration test that simulates streaming tiny tasks, 3) broaden telemetry around per-job inflight counters. I'll add all to the scheduler epic.

maya (infra): can someone schedule a 30-min postmortem tomorrow? want to include cost runbook and a mitigation playbook for noisy shard jobs.

leo (serving): I'll create the postmortem doc and invite scheduler, infra, and ml infra.

ops-oncall: note — leaving the temporary throttle in place until the hotfix is canaried and we validate. Will revert after green.

maya (infra): great work everyone.

darren (scheduler): thanks — will follow up with timelines in the PR comments. :white_check_mark:
